chunks: Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir and Abdul Karim ibn Amr, from Abdul Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entrusted Ali (peace be upon him) with a thousand doors, each word and each door opening to a thousand words and a thousand doors.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet entrust to Imam Ali regarding the doors of knowledge?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq describing the Prophet’s bequest of a thousand 'doors' of knowledge to Imam Ali, a metaphor for the infinite, layered depth of divine wisdom (*hikmah*) and esoteric interpretation (*ta'wil*) transmitted to the Imams. This narration underscores the Shia belief that the Imamate is the custodian of the Quran's inner dimensions, extending beyond the literal text to encompass the totality of prophetic insight.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-34 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father, Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Jabir and Abdul Karim ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdul Hameed ibn Abil Daylam that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,
“God’s Prophet (MGB) entrusted Ali (MGB) with a thousand doors each of which opened up to one-thousand words and doors.”
